text:
maya: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change I'm seeing a 12% p95 regression on small-chat runs. Did an nsys capture and there is one new hotspot that looks like a fallback GEMM instead of the fused matmul+softmax kernel.

liam: ugh. which commit?

maya: d3f8b2c — the selector now prefers 'compatibility' path for sequences <= 32 if quantized. We probably mis-classified a fastpath case.

rohan: can you paste the nsys command you used? I'll pull the trace.

maya: ran:```bash
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt -o /tmp/run1 dbench --model chat-7b --seq 32 --batch 1
```
Captured timeline: https://perf.internal/runs/176543/run1 (perfetto view)

liam: seeing same on my machine. In perfetto the kernel timeline shows a 1.8ms kernel (matmul_fallback) that previously was ~0.2ms fused.

jen: quick thought: could KV cache lookups change sequence-length distribution? if more prefix hits, effective seq for matmuls is larger and selector flips.

maya: good call. I instrumented kvcache hit rates — they are ~85% for the dataset but there's a short burst where it's 60% (QA prompt). selector used static windowing so it mis-predicted.

rohan: we should add NVTX ranges for: request:start, selector:decision, kernel:launch(name), kvcache:lookup(hit/miss). that'll make these timelines searchable without manual log cross refs.

liam: agreed. naming suggestions: keep ranges short and deterministic. propose:```
NVTX: push("req:/<model>@<ver>")
NVTX: push("sel:fastpath|quantized") or push("sel:fallback")
NVTX: push("k:kernname") // avoid embedding heap addresses or request ids
NVTX: push("kv:hit") / push("kv:miss")
```
We should avoid including variable tokens like full UUIDs — use tags only.

jen: +1 on tag-only. Also prefer hierarchical names for perf queries: req/model/version then child ranges for selector/kernel so perf tools can aggregate easily.

maya: small perf optimization idea: selector can consult a short moving-average of effective_seq (seq - kv_prefix_hits) instead of static seq; that would prevent flipping on short bursts.

rohan: can we do an A/B behind a feature flag? change selector to MA-based in canary and add the NVTX ranges in the canary binary, then run identical nsys traces and compare.

maya: plan: 1) add NVTX ranges (lightweight push/pop) around selector and kernel-launch (PR now), 2) add MA logic behind flag (PR after), 3) run 50 nsys profiles on canary vs main, 4) compare p50/p95 and perfetto histograms.

liam: for the NVTX calls, keep them conditional on a runtime env var so we don't pay cost in production unless enabled. eg:```c++
if (nvtx_enabled) { nvtxRangePushA(name); }
...
if (nvtx_enabled) { nvtxRangePop(); }
```
Also add a short macro helper to sanitize names (strip spaces, clamp length 64).

perf-bot: Reminder: when uploading nsys captures, include `--sample=none` and the `.qdrep` size limit note in the run ticket.

jen: one more: for kernel names prefer stable canonical labels (e.g., matmul_fused_v2) not runtime-generated kernel symbol names; we can map symbols to canonical names in our postprocess script.

maya: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/4582 (nvtx ranges + env gating). Putting canary label "nvtx-selector-ma".

rohan: I'll queue perf runs once PR is merged. + I'll write a perf dashboard panel showing 'time spent in sel:fallback' vs 'sel:fastpath' per request.

liam: sounds good. if MA fix removes the 1.8ms hotspot we're golden. thanks for triage @maya :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy queued: branch=nvtx-selector-ma env=canary owner=rohan ci:passed

maya: leaving notes in PR about not logging request IDs and about max name length.

jen: TL;DR: add NVTX ranges, keep names tag-only & canonical, gate on env var, try MA-based selector behind feature flag, run A/B nsys captures and analyze perfetto histograms.

liam: feel free to ping me if you want me to eyeball the perfetto traces live.

maya: will do — thanks all.
